review: Having played pool at competitive level having participated in national championships, this Virtual Pool series always has been my favourite simulation of the game. Virtual Pool 4 is by far the best with an extremely accurate physics engine that brings it as close to real pool as possible. Once you adjust to mouse-based controls, there is remarkably fine control over the cue ball, responsive, predicable and accurate reactions from others balls, cushions and spin. I found playing this game I could apply the same patterns, shots and strategies I used in the real world, making it immensely enjoyable. There is a wide variety of games and disciplines and career modes to keep you entertained and an evergreen install on my gaming machines. The AI can feel a little unbalanced, at times easily running the table with impossible shots only miss a sitter at an attempt to simulate missing under pressure. But if you look past that you cannot really do much better than the Virtual Pool series for your pool simulation needs. Take a bow Celeris!

VP4 still has no real competitors in 2026. 

It is a highly realistic simulation, with a ton of game rules, educational material and campaign modes on top. You could spend a lifetime playing this without getting bored. 

If it ain't broke, don't fix it. That said, it still receives substantial updates a decade later. This is Celeris's whole portfolio, and has been for 30 years; not a one-off from some fly-by-night game developer. This is the MS Flight Simulator of billiards.

It runs at 120+ FPS at any resolution on a potato and looks fantastic. Every other pool game I've seen or tried has poorer physics, poorer controls, poorer performance, and fewer options.

It appears the few competitors that exist want to skip the hard stuff and compete primarily on either the multiplayer experience (something I personally have not tried and have no interest in it), or graphics. On the latter point, believe it or not, there is not much room for improvement: the fact that billiards shapes are mostly mathematical primitives like spheres, planes, and cylinders makes rendering this stuff realistically trivial, they are what GPUs are designed around; slap some nice textures and good lighting on, and there is very little room for graphical improvement. The more "modern" titles use a lot of post processing, environments, and other gimmicks to "sweeten" the look, but this always comes at an unjustified cost to performance and comes across as more "theatrical" than "realistic" (and to my eye it often makes everything look like it's coated in Vaseline and sitting next to a fog machine). I would choose the clean look of VP4 every time, and high framerates are far more important for realism in a game like this than all those gimmicks, anyway. 

There are certainly improvements that could be made to the UI and other ancillary aspects of the game. More game rules, campaign options, and exercises are always possible and welcome, even though they are already exceedingly copious. But no other game comes close; VP4 is still worth double or triple the asking price, and is unlikely to be superseded by anything but VP5.

Virtual Pool 4 is a deeply simulation-focused cue sports game developed and published by Celeris that positions itself less as a casual sports title and more as a serious digital recreation of real-world billiards. As the fourth main entry in a long-running series, it builds on decades of refinement with a clear emphasis on physics accuracy, rule authenticity, and player skill development. Rather than chasing flashy presentation or arcade-style shortcuts, Virtual Pool 4 is designed for players who want an experience that mirrors the nuances, discipline, and mental precision of playing pool and snooker in real life.

The foundation of the experience lies in its physics system, which remains the game’s most defining strength. Ball behavior responds convincingly to spin, speed, angle, and cue placement, allowing for advanced techniques such as draw shots, follow-through, masse, and precise English to behave in ways that feel grounded and predictable once learned. Collisions between balls and cushions are calculated with care, giving each shot a sense of weight and consequence that rewards thoughtful planning over improvisation. This commitment to realism means the game has a steeper learning curve than more casual pool titles, but it also makes every successful shot deeply satisfying, especially when executing complex positional play or delicate safety shots.

Variety is another area where Virtual Pool 4 excels. The game includes an extensive list of cue sport disciplines, ranging from familiar staples like 8-ball, 9-ball, and straight pool to more specialized formats such as one-pocket, bank pool, rotation, snooker, and lesser-known regional variants. Each mode comes with customizable rule sets, allowing players to toggle between casual pub-style rules and strict professional regulations. Table sizes, pocket difficulty, shot calling, handicaps, and fouls can all be adjusted, making the experience adaptable to both newcomers experimenting with the basics and experienced players looking to replicate tournament conditions.

Beyond individual matches, Virtual Pool 4 provides structured progression through multiple career paths. The Pro Tour mode places players in a competitive ladder against AI opponents, tracking rankings, performance, and consistency across seasons. This mode captures the steady grind of competitive cue sports, where improvement comes incrementally through discipline and practice rather than dramatic leaps. The Hustler career mode offers a slightly more narrative-driven alternative, focusing on high-stakes matches, bankroll management, and reputation building. Together, these modes add context and motivation to long-term play, giving players reasons to refine their skills beyond simple exhibition matches.

For players new to cue sports, the game includes an extensive tutorial and training suite that sets it apart from most sports simulations. Video lessons and practice drills explain not just how to perform shots, but why they work, covering concepts like cue ball control, tangent lines, spin effects, and defensive play. These lessons transform the game into a genuine learning tool, capable of improving real-world understanding of billiards mechanics. While the instructional approach may feel dense or slow-paced to some, it aligns perfectly with the game’s philosophy of mastery through knowledge and repetition.

Visually, Virtual Pool 4 is functional rather than modern. Tables, balls, and environments are rendered clearly enough to support gameplay accuracy, but menus and interface elements reflect older design sensibilities. Navigation can feel rigid, and presentation lacks the polish and spectacle seen in newer sports titles. However, this restraint also keeps distractions to a minimum, allowing players to focus entirely on shot execution and strategic thinking. Audio design follows a similar philosophy, emphasizing subtle table sounds and minimal ambiance rather than dramatic commentary or music.

Multiplayer functionality extends the game’s lifespan by allowing players to compete online in ranked matches, tournaments, and casual games. These features appeal particularly to dedicated cue sport fans looking for serious competition, though setup and interface elements can feel dated compared to modern online systems. Still, the ability to track statistics, participate in leagues, and test skills against real opponents reinforces the game’s simulation-first identity.

Overall, Virtual Pool 4 stands as one of the most authentic cue sports simulations available on PC. Its dedication to realistic physics, expansive rule sets, and educational depth makes it less accessible to casual players seeking quick entertainment, but exceptionally rewarding for those willing to invest time and patience. While its aging interface and understated presentation may limit its broader appeal, the quality of its core mechanics ensures it remains a benchmark title for billiards enthusiasts. For players who value realism, technical precision, and the satisfaction of mastering a complex sport, Virtual Pool 4 delivers an experience that feels closer to practice at a real table than a traditional video game.
